chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ali ibn Isma'il al-Daghshi from a man from the people of Syria from Abd Allah ibn Aban al-Zayyat from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who married his paternal uncle's daughter, and his paternal grandfather's concubine had breastfed him. Is she prohibited to the boy or not? He said: No. This is a continuous, disconnected report, and its ruling is that it is not raised against the continuous, authentic reports with sound chains. And if it were accepted, it would be interpreted as meaning that if the concubine had breastfed him with the milk of the grandfather (not the father), or if she had breastfed him with a type of breastfeeding that does not cause prohibition. And if it were complete breastfeeding, the uncle would have become a relative (prohibited) if the grandfather was from the father's side, and if the grandfather was from the mother's side, there is no basis for prohibition there.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: concubine (mother of a child from the master)
key_terms.خَبَرٌ مَقْطُوعٌ مُرْسَلٌ: a continuous but disconnected report (weak chain)

ai.seo_question: Does a concubine's breastfeeding prohibit a man from marrying his cousin?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the breastfeeding of a concubine (umm walad) does not create a prohibitive kinship (mahram) with her son, as the milk is not considered 'complete' or direct enough to establish the same bond as the father's milk. He explains that this weak (mursal) report is either interpreted as non-prohibitive breastfeeding or, even if complete, only establishes the uncle as a milk-brother rather than a direct impediment, thereby preserving the validity of the marriage.
